correctness.rationale: For any positive-definite quadratic pullback A realizing distortion K, normalize N(x)^2 ≤ xᵀAx ≤ K²N(x)^2. Coordinate sign-averaging preserves each inequality and makes A diagonal. Its entries are ≥1 by singleton coordinate tests; hence Euclidean squared norm is bounded above by K²N(x)^2. Taking A=I gives equality, so the global real Banach–Mazur minimum equals sup ||x||₂²/N(x)². Substituting t_i=x_i² gives a bounded finite primal LP; its exact dual is fractional set cover. Clique/stable-set duality proves the graph formula. For perfect graphs the fractional chromatic number is integral; for odd holes and antiholes matching LP witnesses yield noninteger values m/2 and m/k, and the strong perfect graph theorem supplies the converse. The included checker verified all 64 four-vertex graphs via exact rational primal/dual enumeration and seven matched certificates, including the seven-vertex antihole. This finite evidence is illustrative, not a substitute for the general proof. No external computation is logically necessary.

originality.rationale: Fakhoury arXiv:2305.13125v1 defines the exact 2-convexified family but studies isometries; its Theorem 1.1 does not optimize Banach–Mazur distance. arXiv:2404.01733v1 concerns combinatorial sum norms, and arXiv:2605.14072v1 characterizes perfect graphs through Banach-duality/extreme-point phenomena rather than the Euclidean Hilbert distance of quadratic norms. Published result da23138814f6 proves the analogous fractional-cover value only for the canonical map of the sum norm into ℓ1, explicitly excluding arbitrary isomorphisms and Banach–Mazur distance. The new sign-conjugation averaging theorem eliminates all non-diagonal ellipsoids and, crucially, proves optimality of the Euclidean norm among unrestricted real-linear isomorphisms. No directly identical or stronger statement was located in source-focused and cross-formulation searches; equivalent unindexed literature is a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: A general unconditional-space comparison theorem or unindexed paper might imply the Euclidean optimality lemma without the same title or parameters.
Not all 33 pages of Fakhoury or all sections of secondary literature were line-by-line inspected; the directly relevant definitions, principal theorem, and term searches were checked.
The induced-subgraph perfectness characterization uses the existing strong perfect graph theorem and has novelty only as a consequence of the new Hilbert metric representation.

value.rationale: The same finite hereditary norms studied in the motivating 2023 primary source now admit an exact, unrestricted distance to Euclidean space for every dimension and every nontransitive combinatorial family. Optimality against all rotated and anisotropic Hilbert norms is substantive beyond the canonical ℓ1 identity result. The formula converts a continuous ellipsoid optimization into a rational fractional set-cover LP, giving a unified class of exact Banach invariants and a graph-perfectness characterization through integrality on all induced coordinate subspaces. It is a natural complete classification and an invariant-to-combinatorics bridge; the 5-cycle and anti-7-cycle fractional values show distinctions not captured by clique size alone. No speculative downstream theorem is required for the value judgment.
